Pack a natality file into compact, lossless, sharded Parquet

Source: R/parquet.R
natality_pack.Rd

Profiles every record, writes one Parquet file per value of shard_by, and then checks that the original records can be rebuilt exactly from the shards (see natality_verify()).

Usage

natality_pack(
  file,
  out_dir,
  shard_by = "DOB_MM",
  level = 22L,
  row_group_size = 1e+06,
  sort_by = NULL,
  int_codes = FALSE,
  parquet_version = c("V1", "V2"),
  max_mb = 95,
  verify = TRUE,
  record_length = NULL,
  memory_limit = "8GB",
  year = 2025
)

Arguments

file

Path to the fixed-width natality file.

out_dir

Directory for the shards and storage.csv. Its base name is used as the stem of the shard file names.

shard_by

Field to shard on. The default, birth month, gives 12 files (plus one for blank months, if any). NULL writes a single file.

level

zstd compression level, 1-22. High levels are slow to write but not slower to read.

row_group_size

Rows per Parquet row group.

sort_by

Columns to sort rows by within each shard. NULL uses natality_default_sort(); character(0) means no sorting.

int_codes

Also store digit-only categorical codes (e.g. MEDUC, MRACE15) as integers. FALSE keeps them as the character codes that label_natality() expects.

parquet_version

"V1" (most widely readable) or "V2".

max_mb

Warn if any shard is larger than this many MiB.

verify

Run natality_verify() after writing.

record_length

Record length of the file, excluding line endings. NULL detects it from the first 10,000 records; every record must then have that length.

memory_limit

DuckDB memory limit, e.g. "8GB".

year

Data year; see natality_years().

Value

Invisibly, a list with storage (the storage table), report (from natality_report()) and verified (TRUE, FALSE, or NA if not run).

How fields are stored

The storage of each field is decided from the data, not assumed from the guide:

  • int: digits only, zero-padded to full width. Stored as the smallest integer type that fits; rebuilt by padding with 0. Used for numeric fields, and for digit-only codes too if int_codes = TRUE.

  • left: no leading blanks. Stored as trimmed text; rebuilt by padding on the right.

  • right: no trailing blanks. Stored as trimmed text; rebuilt by padding on the left.

  • raw: anything else. Stored untrimmed.

  • blank: a FILLER that is blank in every record. Not stored.

A blank field is stored as NULL. The rules are written to <out_dir>/storage.csv, which natality_verify() and natality_unpack() need, so keep it with the shards. Numeric fields keep their sentinel codes (DBWT 9999, CIG_0 99, ...); turn them into NA when analysing.

Bytes beyond the record length the guide documents (1330 for 2025) are kept as a trailing column, FILLER_1331, unless they are blank in every record.

What is not kept

Record order (rows are sorted so that they compress better) and line endings. The check compares the source and the rebuilt records as multisets.

File size

GitHub blocks files over 100 MiB and warns at 50 MiB, so max_mb defaults to 95.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- natality_pack("Nat2025PublicUS.c20260624.r20260922.txt", "nat2025")
res$report
arrow::open_dataset("nat2025")
} # }
